steps.why: It reads the free text of the data to flag instructions aimed at the reviewer, so the text must stay on the machine
It reads customer notes, payment references and list remarks and returns risk signals with the exact text span
Applying the approved definitions to many fields at once and citing the rows it rests on is the hardest step
It checks the recommendation against the evidence after code has re-read every cited fact from Zetaris
It argues against a close before it can stand
It checks a draft meant for a customer for tipping-off wording, on top of fixed patterns
Keeps a step answering when Nightshift fails; the same model as the local steps

brier_definition: Mean of (confidence - y) squared over cases, where y is 1 when the chosen outcome is acceptable for the case (its expected or an acceptable outcome) and 0 otherwise. 0 is perfect; always answering with confidence 0.5 scores 0.25. Lower is better.
